questions.question: A model performs extremely well on training data but poorly on unseen test data. This situation is called:
Which statement best describes underfitting?
options: The model memorizes noise in the training data.
The model is too simple and fails to capture important patterns.
The model performs perfectly on all datasets.
The model uses too many features.

questions.question: The Bias-Variance Tradeoff mainly involves balancing:
A highly complex model generally tends to have:
A linear model trying to classify highly nonlinear data is most likely suffering from:
Which technique is specifically designed to estimate how well a model will generalize to unseen data?
In 5-fold cross-validation, the dataset is divided into:
options: One training set and one testing set only

questions.question: During k-fold cross-validation, each data point is used for testing:
Why is cross-validation generally preferred over a single train-test split?
options: It uses multiple evaluations and reduces dependence on one random split.
It reduces the number of features.

questions.question: Which scenario best represents feature engineering?
options: Creating a new feature 'Age Group' from the 'Age' column

questions.question: Why can good feature engineering significantly improve model performance?
options: Because it changes the algorithm itself
Because it provides more meaningful information to the model

questions.question: Adding too many irrelevant features often leads to:
A model with very high bias usually has:
options: Poor performance on both training and testing data
Excellent performance on training data only

questions.question: Suppose a model gets 99% training accuracy but only 60% testing accuracy. Which statement is most reasonable?
options: The model likely suffers from high variance.
The model has achieved perfect generalization.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of feature extraction?
options: Splitting data into training and testing sets
Converting a date into 'day of week' and 'month' features

questions.question: What is the primary goal of the Bias-Variance Tradeoff?
options: Find a balance that minimizes generalization error

questions.question: In k-fold cross-validation, if k becomes very large (for example, equal to the number of samples), the method is called:
Which statement about feature engineering is FALSE?
options: It may involve creating new variables from existing data.
It is completely independent of domain knowledge.
It can help reveal hidden patterns.

questions.question: A data scientist reduces the number of features because the model memorizes noise in the training data. This action primarily attempts to reduce:
Which sequence best represents a good machine learning workflow?
options: Collect data → Engineer features → Cross-validate → Select model
Deploy model → Collect data → Train model
Create features → Skip testing → Increase complexity
